key_insight: Transporting a simple log-concave source to heavy-tailed or well-separated multimodal targets intrinsically requires large gradients, regardless of the generative model’s architecture.
engineering_relevance: These gradient barriers create expressivity–stability trade-offs that architecture or training changes alone may not resolve.
method: Derive quantitative gradient and Jacobian lower bounds for pushforward maps.
Establish barriers under weaker regularity assumptions and target perturbations.
Propose bijective reparametrizations to reduce gradient demands in density approximation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments support the theoretical analysis, but the abstract provides no datasets, metrics, or effect sizes.
watch_item: The reparametrization mitigation concerns density approximation and should not be assumed to remove barriers in generative sampling.
paper_title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
